summary: The phase's work was in the tree but never committed, which is what the gate flagged. I committed it as one commit, f424190, and the tree is clean. Getting it through the pre-commit hook meant fixing a second problem: the hook exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, which pointed the test suite's git calls at the outer repository's index. The test helpers now strip it.
commits: f424190 An unborn HEAD runs the full suite instead of exiting 2

tests.explained: Count is the sum of cargo's per-binary 'test result' lines: 462 unit, 9, 35, 13, 30 and 76 integration. The 24 new tests are the phase's tests (git, closure, run, impacted_tests, changed_symbols). None are skipped, ignored or deleted. fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test and `make review-quick` pass. The prek hook (fmt, clippy, cargo test) passed on the final commit. The suite also passes with a bogus GIT_INDEX_FILE exported.

design: Design as briefed and unchanged. New code: `Git::head_is_unborn`, `Reason::UnbornHead`, and an `impacted_run` check that runs before any diff or tyf lookup. The only addition in this fix is test-side isolation. `src/git.rs` unit tests call a `drop_hook_git_env` once (a `Once` that removes `pytest::LOCAL_GIT_ENV` from the process env). `tests/common/mod.rs` gets `strip_hook_git_env`, applied to its `TestRepo::git` and gerenuk commands. In `tests/run.rs` it is applied to `without_tools`, the hook fixture's `git()` and the first-commit test's `git commit`.
real_run:
Ran the debug build in a fresh tempdir repo with an unborn HEAD and staged files.
- `run --dry-run --format json`: exit 0, decision `run_all`, reason `unborn_head`.
- `impacted-tests --format json`: exit 0, `run_all` / `unborn_head`, base `HEAD`, empty `impacted_tests`.
- `changed-symbols`: exit 2, "HEAD has no commit yet, so there is nothing to diff against...", no `origin/main`.
- `run --base nope --dry-run`: exit 2, `no usable base ref (tried nope). Pass --base with a ref that exists.`

With the dry-run JSON format, gerenuk also printed a "pytest not found on PATH" line on stderr. It still exited 0. That is not covered by the brief and I did not investigate it.
deviations: Beyond the brief: the test helpers now strip the hook's git env. The prek cargo-test hook runs the suite with GIT_INDEX_FILE exported, and several tests failed there (the replay-worktree unit tests, the linked-worktree tests, the hook fixtures). That blocked the commit, and I did not use --no-verify. Only test code changed for this; production behaviour is untouched.

Replacing an earlier approach: I first tried a `git` shim script for the unit tests. It hit 'Text file busy' (ETXTBSY) when tests ran in parallel, so I used a one-time `std::env::remove_var` instead (safe in edition 2021).
unresolved_issues: During testing I exported a fake GIT_INDEX_FILE and ran the commit. That corrupted this repo's index (invalid cache-tree). I repaired it with `git read-tree HEAD`. The working tree was never touched and the final commit and hook passed. A dangling object warning may remain in `git fsck`.

The `Git` production spawn in `src/git.rs` still inherits the hook's git env, so `replay` inside a hook could hit the same `GIT_INDEX_FILE` problem. This was not in the fix brief and I did not change it.
A stray stderr line appeared on the dry-run JSON path in a repo with no pytest on PATH (see real_run). It is unconfirmed whether this is pre-existing.
